description: SigLIP 2 so400m at 384px. The highest-leverage model in the stack: one embedding powers search, near-duplicate refinement, diversity constraints and zero-shot tagging.

license.training_data: WebLI (Google internal web-scale image-text). Terms are the model card's, not a separate dataset licence.
license.note: Desk assessment only. Apache-2.0 on the model card; not verified at source.

notes:
SigLIP 2 uses a sigmoid loss rather than CLIP's softmax contrastive loss, so raw logits are not comparable to CLIP's and any threshold tuned on a CLIP model must be re-tuned. Stretch resize rather than centre crop is deliberate: cropping loses the edges of a composition, and composition is part of what we score.

NO ONNX AT THE DECLARED SOURCE (checked 2026-08-17 via the HF API). google/siglip2-so400m-patch14-384 publishes safetensors only, so there is no siglip2-so400m-patch14-384-vision.onnx to download and scripts/models/fetch_weights.py reports this entry UNAVAILABLE. source_url stays the provenance page rather than being repointed at something plausible: the two ways to actually get this file are to export the vision tower locally from the safetensors, or to adopt the third-party conversion at onnx-community/siglip2-so400m-patch14-384-ONNX. The conversion is NOT a URL edit -- its graph exposes last_hidden_state and pooler_output where this config binds `image_embeds`, and its fp32 vision tower is 1.7GB against this config's declared fp16 -- so adopting it changes `outputs`, `quantization` and the embedding that every stored vector lives in, which is an eval-harness decision, not a fetch. The repository is NOT gated (HF API reports gated:false), so no token is involved either way.

BATCHING (issue #31): DEMOTED TO 1, UNVERIFIED. This entry declared supported=true, max_batch=16, dynamic_axes=true. weights.blake3 is null, so the ONNX graph it names has never been produced or hashed, let alone had its input shape read -- the claim was an assumption wearing the clothes of a measurement, which is the same defect issue #31 found in the YuNet entry. Restore it by running onnxruntime.InferenceSession(...).get_inputs()[0].shape against the pinned checkpoint and recording that in batching.verified_against. Declining to batch costs throughput and nothing else.
